- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slightly rising, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per subsequent period to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model often underestimates upside; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean to capture policy-driven rally.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid false optimism.  
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (≥3/30d) and sentiment is mixed, model tends to overfit recent highs; apply a 1–2% downward bias to smooth out volatility.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is above 70; forecast should trend downward 0.5–1% per period until reversion.  
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model often overestimates volatility; cap forecast range within ±1.5% of 30d moving average to avoid extreme outliers.
